subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <algorithm> header. Phase 10 (2026-05-13) shipped 89 algorithms: non-modifying sequence ops, modifying ops (copy/move/fill/transform/generate/remove/replace families), rearrangement (iter_swap/swap_ranges/reverse/rotate/shift_left/shift_right/shuffle/sample/unique), sort (introsort) + stable_sort (no-buffer in-place merge, O(N log^2 N)), binary search, partition + stable_partition (allocator-free O(N log N)), heap, set operations, min/max/clamp, comparison, and permutation. Three deferrals: ranges:: overloads (await <ranges>), parallel-execution-policy overloads (await <execution>), lexicographical_compare_three_way (awaits <compare>).
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <algorithm> header. 89 algorithms shipped 2026-05-13 (Phase 10) covering non-modifying / modifying / rearrangement / sort / binary search / partition / heap / set ops / min-max / comparison / permutation. ranges:: overloads, parallel exec policies, and lexicographical_compare_three_way deferred.

symbols.name: all_of
symbols.notes: Vacuously true for empty range; short-circuits on first false. std C++11 only because that is when it was added; back-ported (no language feature blocker).

symbols.name: any_of
symbols.notes: False for empty range; short-circuits on first true. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: none_of
symbols.notes: Vacuously true for empty range. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: for_each
symbols.notes: Returns f by value (NRVO + copy elision keep this efficient on every tier). C++11 std uses move(f); semantically equivalent for non-throwing functors. Sequential ordering only on this no-policy overload.

symbols.name: for_each_n
symbols.notes: Counted variant; returns iterator past last visited element. Back-ported to C++98 (counted loop, no blocker).

symbols.name: count
symbols.notes: Return type iterator_traits<It>::difference_type. Returns 0 for empty range.

symbols.name: count_if
symbols.notes: Predicate variant; same difference_type return.

symbols.name: mismatch
symbols.notes: Four overloads: 3-arg vs 4-arg x default == vs custom pred. The 4-arg forms (two explicit ranges) are C++14 in std; restd back-ports them to C++98. Returns pair<It1, It2>.

symbols.name: find
symbols.notes: Linear search; returns last on miss.

symbols.name: find_if
symbols.notes: Linear search with predicate.

symbols.name: find_if_not
symbols.notes: Inverse of find_if; back-ported to C++98 (pure predicate negation).

symbols.name: find_end
symbols.notes: Last occurrence of needle as subsequence. Two overloads. Empty-needle returns last1 per std (note asymmetry vs search).

symbols.name: find_first_of
symbols.notes: O(N*M) naive scan (matches std). Two overloads.

symbols.name: adjacent_find
symbols.notes: First adjacent pair satisfying ==/pred. Two overloads.

symbols.name: search
symbols.notes: First occurrence of needle as subsequence. Two C++98 overloads (default == / pred). Empty-needle returns first1 (asymmetry with find_end is std-mandated). O(N*M) naive.

symbols.name: search (searcher overload)
symbols.notes: C++17 form search(first, last, searcher) delegates to the searcher callable. Ships at C++98 (the overload itself has no language blocker; concrete searcher types live in <functional> and are deferred there).

symbols.name: search_n
symbols.notes: First run of count consecutive equal elements. Two overloads. count <= 0 returns first per LWG 426.

symbols.name: copy
symbols.notes: Returns one past last copied. Source and destination must not overlap unless d_first is outside [first, last).

symbols.name: copy_if
symbols.notes: Predicate-filtered copy. Back-ported to C++98 (no language blocker).

symbols.name: copy_n
symbols.notes: Counted copy. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: copy_backward
symbols.notes: Walks in reverse; safe when source and destination overlap and d_last lies inside (first, last]. Returns iterator to new beginning.

symbols.name: move (algorithm)
symbols.notes: Cannot be back-ported to C++98 (a copy fallback would silently change move-only-type semantics). Coexists with restd::move (the utility cast) via overload resolution (one arg vs three).

symbols.name: move_backward
symbols.notes: Same gating rationale as move (algorithm). Bidirectional iterators required.

symbols.name: fill
symbols.notes: Assigns value to every element.

symbols.name: fill_n
symbols.notes: restd always ships the C++11 iterator-returning signature on every tier; C++98 callers can ignore the return.

symbols.name: transform
symbols.notes: Unary and binary overloads. Unary allows in-place transform (d_first may equal first).

symbols.name: generate
symbols.notes: Calls g() to fill the range; g may carry state across calls.

symbols.name: generate_n
symbols.notes: Always ships the C++11 iterator-returning signature on every tier.

symbols.name: remove
symbols.notes: In-place compaction. C++11 strengthened kept-element transfer to move; restd matches per-tier (copy on C++98, move on C++11+). Returns one past last kept; tail is valid-but-unspecified (erase-remove idiom).

symbols.name: remove_if
symbols.notes: Predicate variant of remove; same per-tier move/copy gating.

symbols.name: remove_copy
symbols.notes: Out-of-place; pure copy semantics (no conditional move dance).

symbols.name: remove_copy_if
symbols.notes: Predicate variant of remove_copy.

symbols.name: replace
symbols.notes: In-place value-based replacement.

symbols.name: replace_if
symbols.notes: Predicate variant of replace.

symbols.name: replace_copy
symbols.notes: Out-of-place sibling of replace.

symbols.name: replace_copy_if
symbols.notes: Out-of-place sibling of replace_if.

symbols.name: iter_swap
symbols.notes: ADL-friendly: using restd::swap; swap(*a, *b); — picks up user-supplied swap via ADL.

symbols.name: swap_ranges
symbols.notes: Parallel element-wise swap of two ranges.

symbols.name: reverse
symbols.notes: In-place two-pointer reversal. Bidirectional iterators required.

symbols.name: reverse_copy
symbols.notes: Out-of-place sibling of reverse.

symbols.name: rotate
symbols.notes: restd always ships the C++11 iterator-returning signature. Forward-iterator algorithm via swap-walk with manually eliminated tail recursion (per Stepanov & McJones, Elements of Programming).

symbols.name: rotate_copy
symbols.notes: Out-of-place rotate; two inlined copy loops to keep the file independent of copy.hpp.

symbols.name: shift_left
symbols.notes: Back-ported to C++98 (forward walk with assignment). Per-tier move/copy gating like remove.

symbols.name: shift_right
symbols.notes: DEVIATION FROM STD: requires BidirectionalIterator (std requires only ForwardIterator). Forward-only algorithm is essentially a hidden rotate and was judged not worth the niche path.

symbols.name: shuffle
symbols.notes: Fisher-Yates with unbiased rejection sampling against a caller-supplied URBG. No <random> dependency. Back-ported to C++98 by relaxing the URBG parameter to lvalue reference. NOT constexpr — URBG state mutation is canonically constexpr-hostile.

symbols.name: sample
symbols.notes: Tag-dispatched: forward iterator -> Knuth Algorithm S (preserves input order); input iterator -> Vitter Algorithm R (reservoir). No <random> dependency. NOT constexpr.

symbols.name: unique
symbols.notes: Collapses consecutive duplicates. Per-tier move/copy gating like remove. Two overloads (default == / pred).

symbols.name: unique_copy
symbols.notes: Out-of-place; uses saved-local approach (requires CopyConstructible + CopyAssignable value type) rather than std s 3-form tag-dispatch. Two overloads.

symbols.name: sort
symbols.notes: Introsort: median-of-3 + Lomuto partition; heapsort fallback at depth 2*floor(log2(N)); insertion sort below 16 elements. Tail-recurses on the larger half (O(log N) stack). NOT constexpr (matches std through C++26).

symbols.name: stable_sort
symbols.notes: Bottom-up merge sort with no-buffer in-place merge (asymmetric lower_bound/upper_bound preserves stability). O(N log^2 N) worst-case allocator-free; std s typical implementation uses get_temporary_buffer for O(N log N) when allocation succeeds. NOT constexpr.

symbols.name: partial_sort
symbols.notes: Heap-based, O(N log k). Inlines a private _sift_down_ helper; cleanup ticket to call restd::make_heap/sort_heap when those are refactored. NOT constexpr.

symbols.name: partial_sort_copy
symbols.notes: Out-of-place sibling of partial_sort; heap-based, O(N log min(N,M)). NOT constexpr.

symbols.name: is_sorted
symbols.notes: Built on is_sorted_until; range is sorted iff until-iterator equals last.

symbols.name: is_sorted_until
symbols.notes: First out-of-order position. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: nth_element
symbols.notes: Introselect: quickselect with median-of-3 + Lomuto, heap-based fallback at depth 2*floor(log2(N)). Average O(N), worst O(N log N). NOT constexpr.

symbols.name: lower_bound
symbols.notes: First position not less than value. O(log N) comparisons on every iterator category; O(log N) stepping on random access, O(N) on forward.

symbols.name: upper_bound
symbols.notes: First position strictly greater than value.

symbols.name: equal_range
symbols.notes: Returns pair(lower_bound, upper_bound). Pivot-then-bounded-scan implementation does strictly fewer comparisons than two separate calls.

symbols.name: binary_search
symbols.notes: Built on lower_bound; checks the found position is actually equivalent.

symbols.name: is_partitioned
symbols.notes: Skip leading trues, verify suffix all-false. Vacuously true for empty / one-element. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: partition
symbols.notes: DEVIATION FROM STD C++11+: requires BidirectionalIterator (std relaxed to ForwardIterator in C++11). Hoare two-cursor scan.

symbols.name: partition_copy
symbols.notes: Splits into two output ranges by predicate. Returns pair of output-end iterators. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: stable_partition
symbols.notes: Recursive split-and-rotate (mirror of stable_sort s no-buffer merge). O(N log N) allocator-free; std s typical impl uses get_temporary_buffer for O(N). Bidirectional iterators required. NOT constexpr.

symbols.name: partition_point
symbols.notes: Binary search variant taking a unary predicate (lower_bound for partitioned ranges). Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: push_heap
symbols.notes: Sift-up; inserts (last - 1) into the heap [first, last - 1). iter_swap-based; a future perf pass could swap in hole-walking (~30% faster for non-trivial types).

symbols.name: pop_heap
symbols.notes: Sift-down; moves the heap max to (last - 1) and restores the heap on the shrunken range.

symbols.name: make_heap
symbols.notes: Bottom-up Floyd construction; O(N) (not O(N log N) as naive N successive push_heaps would be).

symbols.name: sort_heap
symbols.notes: Repeated extract-max into the shrinking tail; O(N log N). Inlines its own _sift_down_ rather than delegating to pop_heap (saves the per-pop length recheck).

symbols.name: is_heap
symbols.notes: Thin wrapper over is_heap_until. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: is_heap_until
symbols.notes: First parent-child pair violating the heap property. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: merge
symbols.notes: Stable merge of two sorted ranges. Stability test: emit right only when STRICTLY less than left.

symbols.name: inplace_merge
symbols.notes: Public lift of stable_sort s private _stable_in_place_merge_. No-buffer divide-and-rotate (Knuth, TAOCP 5.2.4). O((N1+N2) log(min(N1,N2))) allocator-free. NOT constexpr (mirrors std).

symbols.name: includes
symbols.notes: Multiset subsequence test. O(N+M).

symbols.name: set_union
symbols.notes: Multiset union: max(n1, n2) copies per value. Emits range1 s copy on equivalent tie.

symbols.name: set_intersection
symbols.notes: Multiset intersection: min(n1, n2) copies. Drawn from range1.

symbols.name: set_difference
symbols.notes: Multiset difference range1 - range2: max(0, n1 - n2) copies.

symbols.name: set_symmetric_difference
symbols.notes: Multiset XOR: |n1 - n2| copies.

symbols.name: min
symbols.notes: Two-argument forms return const reference. Initializer_list overload (C++11+, gated on D_ENV_CPP_FEATURE_LANG_INITIALIZER_LISTS) returns by value. Returns first arg on tie.

symbols.name: max
symbols.notes: Mirror of min. Returns first arg on tie.

symbols.name: min_element
symbols.notes: First occurrence of the minimum (strict-less update preserves first-of-ties).

symbols.name: max_element
symbols.notes: First occurrence of the maximum.

symbols.name: minmax
symbols.notes: Two-argument forms return pair of const refs. Initializer_list overload gated on C++11+. Returns pair(a, b) on tie. Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: minmax_element
symbols.notes: 3N/2 comparisons via pairwise processing. Asymmetric tie-breaking: min = first occurrence, max = LAST (mandated by std to distinguish from (min_element, max_element)). Back-ported.

symbols.name: clamp
symbols.notes: Returns const ref to v / lo / hi. Precondition !(hi < lo) is caller s responsibility (matches std). Back-ported to C++98.

symbols.name: equal
symbols.notes: Four overloads: 3-arg vs 4-arg x default == vs custom pred. 4-arg forms (C++14 std) back-ported to C++98. 4-arg length-mismatch short-circuit (random-access tag dispatch) deferred — current impl always walks parallel ranges.

symbols.name: lexicographical_compare
symbols.notes: Dictionary-order strict-less. Shorter prefix compares less. Two overloads.

symbols.name: lexicographical_compare_three_way
symbols.notes: Three-way ordering of two ranges. Header placeholder exists; function body deferred pending restd::<compare> (strong_ordering / weak_ordering / partial_ordering).

symbols.name: is_permutation
symbols.notes: Strip matching prefix, then quadratic count-based comparison. Four overloads (3-arg + 4-arg x default == / pred); 4-arg added in C++14 std, back-ported.

symbols.name: next_permutation
symbols.notes: Pandita s algorithm (find rightmost ascent + smallest-larger swap + reverse suffix). O(N). Returns false and rewinds to smallest on wrap.

symbols.name: prev_permutation
symbols.notes: Mirror of next_permutation with comparison flipped.

symbols.name: ranges algorithm overloads
symbols.notes: ranges::find, ranges::sort, ranges::transform, etc. — the constrained range-accepting forms of every algorithm.

symbols.name: ranges fold algorithms
symbols.notes: ranges::fold_left, ranges::fold_right, ranges::fold_left_first, ranges::fold_right_last, plus the *_with_iter variants. Live in <algorithm> in the standard but are exclusively range-based.

symbols.name: parallel-execution-policy overloads
symbols.notes: Overloads taking std::execution::par etc. for the parallelisable algorithms (for_each, transform, reduce, sort, ...).
